description: We are a student team from Nicaragua interested in building a practical and innovative solution for a NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our strengths include electronics, embedded systems, sensors, programming, web development, and prototyping. We are looking for motivated teammates interested in space exploration, data, design, research, or storytelling. Beginners are welcome if they are committed and ready to collaborate. Let’s build something meaningful together!

details:
ARI Cosmos — Artificial Intelligence for Astronaut Health and Mission Safety

ARI Cosmos is an AI-powered platform designed to address one of the greatest challenges of long-duration space exploration: protecting astronaut health and safety when crews are millions of kilometers away from Earth and immediate assistance may be limited.

Our project begins with a fundamental question: How can we help astronauts identify health concerns, anticipate environmental hazards, and prepare to respond before a situation becomes a critical emergency?

ARI: An Intelligent Health Companion for Astronauts

At the heart of the project is ARI, an intelligent space health assistant powered by Google Gemini Live, capable of maintaining natural, real-time voice conversations with astronauts.

ARI allows crew members to report and track physical and emotional indicators, including headaches, dizziness, fatigue, stress, sleep quality, mood, nutrition, and daily habits.

Through scheduled health check-ins, individual crew histories, and mathematical trend analysis, ARI can identify significant changes in recorded indicators and explain potential health concerns using scientific references from NASA.

ARI also enables astronauts to review their personal health histories, monitor changes over time, and receive guidance when certain indicators suggest that additional attention may be necessary.

The goal is not to replace medical professionals or provide definitive diagnoses, but to offer an intelligent support tool that helps astronauts better understand their physical and emotional well-being, especially during extended missions.

Habitat 3D: Preparing for the Hazards of Space

However, protecting astronauts involves more than monitoring their health. It also requires understanding the dangers of the environment surrounding them.

What happens if a solar storm threatens the crew? What if electricity, water, or communication systems fail during a mission to Mars?

To explore these challenges, we developed Habitat 3D, an interactive space habitat simulation and mission safety environment.

Habitat 3D allows users to design and explore conceptual space habitats, configure missions to the Moon or Mars, and investigate different risk scenarios.

Users can examine situations such as solar events, power failures, water supply disruptions, and communication outages, exploring their potential consequences and considering possible response strategies.

Its purpose is to transform complex mission hazards into visual and interactive experiences that support learning, planning, and crew preparedness.

The Connection Between ARI and Habitat 3D: Our Core Innovation

One of the most important features of ARI Cosmos is that ARI and Habitat 3D are not entirely separate tools. They are connected and can work together through artificial intelligence.

An astronaut can begin a natural conversation with ARI and ask it to prepare a space mission simulation.

For example:

"ARI, I want to prepare a mission to Mars. Create a simulation for four astronauts and help me explore the risks of a solar event."

ARI interprets the request and, if essential parameters are missing, asks the user for additional information, such as the mission destination, number of crew members, and mission duration.

Once the required information is available, ARI can directly interact with Habitat 3D's functions to generate and save a simulation, without requiring the astronaut to configure the entire scenario manually.

The user can then open the generated simulation in the three-dimensional environment, explore the habitat, and continue speaking with ARI to understand the scenario's risks and possible protective measures.

AI-generated simulations are organized in a dedicated section, allowing users to revisit them while preserving their manually created habitat designs.

This integration transforms ARI from an assistant that simply provides information into an intelligent interface capable of interacting with another component of the platform and performing concrete actions through voice instructions.

A Comprehensive Vision of Space Mission Safety

ARI Cosmos brings together two essential dimensions of mission safety:

  • Astronaut health and well-being: Tracking physical and emotional indicators, maintaining individual histories, and analyzing health trends.
  • Environmental and mission safety: Exploring space habitats, investigating potential hazards, and interacting with mission simulations.

By connecting these dimensions, ARI Cosmos allows crew members not only to access information but also to participate in scenario preparation and better understand the challenges they may encounter during a mission.

Our Objective

ARI Cosmos is a technological and educational prototype designed to demonstrate how conversational artificial intelligence, health indicator analysis, and interactive three-dimensional simulation can work together to support future space safety technologies.

Although its simulations are conceptual and do not replace certified mission planning systems, the project proposes a more accessible, intuitive, and integrated way of interacting with complex information.

Our vision is that astronauts on future exploration missions could have access to intelligent tools that not only help them recognize changes in their own well-being but also understand the dangers around them and prepare to respond.

ARI supports astronaut health. Habitat 3D helps crews understand and prepare for environmental hazards. Together, they form ARI Cosmos: a platform where artificial intelligence connects human well-being with the safety of space exploration.
